correctness.rationale: The exact zero-sum distance-form decomposition yields the necessary and sufficient Schoenberg threshold. Kernel positivity is independently verified by a two-block spectrum and strict weighted AM–GM. The all-scale derivative factor has an exact endpoint reduction; for every \(m\ge3\) its nontrivial endpoint has a strictly negative third derivative and triple zero at \(p=1\), establishing strict positive derivative. Taylor coefficients and crossover scaling are reconstructed analytically. A standalone independent numerical/exact checker passed 5,273 finite diagnostic assertions, supplementing but not replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is the all-scale strict monotonicity on the entire NONMETRIC negative-type region \(2<b/a\le2m/(m-1)\) for regular-simplex configurations with an equiradial hub, together with the critical centroid small-scale crossover. Gomi–Tsuji Lemma 5.4 already implies the analogous monotonicity on the METRIC region \(b/a\le2\) because the leaf weighting entries are positive, and Roff–Yoshinaga Theorem 3.3 already supplies the algebraic join formula there. Both pre-existing implications are expressly excluded from novelty. No inspected primary source or indexed claim covers the nonmetric range and singular boundary layer; inaccessible full texts and unindexed literature remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The sharp nonmetric negative-type interval \(2<r\le2m/(m-1)\) is a natural complete symmetric subclass where strict all-scale monotonicity survives despite general four-plus-point negative-type semimetric counterexamples. At its geometric centroid endpoint, the one-point magnitude limit jumps from 1 to \((m+1)/2\) and an exact boundary-layer law resolves the noncommuting geometry/scale limits. Together these are a structural positive classification beyond the known metric one-negative-weight theorem, not merely the already-known block-inverse formula.
